title: Radian measure
keyIdea: One radian is the angle at the centre when the arc is as long as the radius, so an angle in radians is arc ÷ radius: θ = s/r. About 6.28 radius-lengths fit round a circle, so a full turn is 2π rad and 180° = π rad. In radians the arc length is simply s = rθ.

kid: Take a piece of string as long as the radius of a circle. Lay it round the edge. The angle it makes at the centre is one radian.
One radian is about 57°. It is a big angle, not a tiny one like 1°.
The whole edge is 2πr long, so about 6.28 strings fit round. A full turn is 2π radians. Half a turn is π radians.
With radians, arc length is easy. An angle of 3 radians on a 4 cm circle has an arc of 3 × 4 = 12 cm.
adult: An angle in radians is the arc length divided by the radius, θ = s/r. It is a ratio of two lengths, so it has no unit and does not depend on the size of the circle.
The circumference is 2πr, so a full turn is 2πr ÷ r = 2π rad. That gives π rad = 180°. To change degrees to radians multiply by π/180; to change back multiply by 180/π. So 135° = 135/180 × π = 3π/4.
Rearranged, s = rθ. This is the degree formula θ/360 × 2πr with the 360 and the 2π already cancelled, which is why calculus and physics use radians.
Common mistakes: dropping the π (writing 135° as 3/4 rad); using the conversion factor upside down; putting degrees into s = rθ; thinking 1 rad is about 1°; and working out r ÷ s instead of s ÷ r.

familyTip: Cut a string as long as the radius of a plate. Walk it round the rim, marking each length. How many fit? Then ask: would a bigger plate fit more strings, or the same number?

worked.title: A circle has radius 8 cm. Find the arc for 135°, then the angle that gives an arc of 20 cm.
steps: For an arc of 20 cm: θ = s ÷ r = 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5 rad.

practice.hint: π rad = 180°, so π/12 rad = 180 ÷ 12 = 15°. Multiply by {k}.

practice.prompt: Find the arc length when r = {r} cm and θ = {=k/2} rad.
practice.hint: θ is already in radians, so use s = rθ with no 360.

choices: The angle where the arc is as long as the radius
The angle where the arc is 1 cm long
practice.hint: A radian compares the arc with the radius of the same circle.
practice.explain: One radian is the angle at the centre when the arc equals the radius. 1/360 of a turn is one degree, and 1 cm depends on the circle's size.

practice.prompt: An arc of {s} cm lies on a circle of radius {r} cm. Find θ in radians.
practice.hint: θ = s ÷ r: how many radius-lengths fit along the arc?
Divide by 180°, then multiply by π.
practice.explain: 135 ÷ 180 = 3/4, and each 180° is π rad, so 135° = 3π/4 ≈ 2.36 rad. Writing 3/4 drops the π.

pool.prompt: How many radians make a full turn?
pool.hint: The edge is 2πr. How many radii is that?
pool.explain: The circumference 2πr divided by r is 2π, so a full turn is 2π ≈ 6.28 rad. π rad is only half a turn.

pool.prompt: An arc of {s} cm makes an angle of {=k/2} rad at the centre. Find the radius in cm.
pool.hint: Rearrange s = rθ: divide the arc by the angle in radians to get r.

pool.prompt: Sam uses s = rθ for a 60° arc with r = 5 cm and gets 5 × 60 = 300 cm. What went wrong?
choices: θ must be in radians: 60° = π/3, so s = 5π/3 ≈ 5.24 cm
pool.hint: s = rθ only works when θ is in radians.
pool.explain: 60° = π/3 rad, so s = 5 × π/3 ≈ 5.24 cm. Putting degrees into s = rθ gives an arc far longer than the whole circle (31.4 cm).

pool.prompt: Convert 1 radian to degrees, to 1 decimal place.

pool.explain: 240/180 = 4/3, so 240° = 4π/3 rad. 4/3 drops the π, and 2π/3 is only 120°.

pool.prompt: Convert 2.5 radians to degrees, to the nearest degree.
Circles of radius 3 cm and 6 cm each have an arc that makes 1.2 rad at the centre. Which is true?
choices: The arcs are 3.6 cm and 7.2 cm, and the angle is the same
The bigger circle's angle is 2.4 rad
pool.hint: Use s = rθ for each circle. Does the angle change?
pool.explain: s = 3 × 1.2 = 3.6 cm and s = 6 × 1.2 = 7.2 cm. The arc doubles with the radius, but s ÷ r is 1.2 rad for both.
